correctness.rationale: The largest prime dividing q−1 cannot cancel in the totient Euler product; for odd q this proves theta=1/3 iff q−1=2^a3^b with a,b>=1. For a primitive g, odd exponent means nonsquare and an odd exponent fails primitivity iff divisible by 3. Thus NSNP membership is precisely exponent 3 mod 6; in particular zero is excluded. The character indicator extended by zero at zero gives main term q−3. For each nontrivial support the chosen split polynomial is not a sixth power; the Weil bound for r distinct roots is (r−1)sqrt(q), and omission of zeros from unused factors changes the complete sum by at most 3−r. The advertised weaker aggregate bound q−648−430sqrt(q) (on 216 times the count) is valid and strictly positive above 186624. A fresh exact computation exhaustively classified all 31 eligible orders through this cutoff, including F_25, F_49 and F_289 using irreducible quadratics t²−2, t²−3 and t²−3 over their respective prime fields. It compared generator-coset and square/cube power membership and found precisely the twelve stated zeros; the nineteen positive counts match the source. The source script was inspected, not executed; the independent finite code and recorded output support only the finite range, while the character bound proves the tail.
residual_risks: No conclusion about arbitrary-density NSNP triples follows; the independent exhaustive computation is confined to the proven finite range and this density.
